newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN FASTEST WITH FLYING FINAL LAP.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN FASTEST WITH FLYING FINAL LAP.

text.p: World champion Michael Doohan put in a flying last lap on Friday to seize provisional pole for Sunday's Italian 500cc motorcycle Grand Prix.

The Australian, winner at the Mugello circuit in rural Tuscany for the past four seasons and leader of this season's championship after three races, pipped Honda team mate Alex Criville of Spain by just 0.025 of a second.
Criville, winner of the most recent race in Spain, had clocked the fastest time on his 20th lap out of 22 and looked to take the overnight honours when rain began to fall.
But the shower was shortlived and triple world champion Doohan did the business on his 21st and last lap out.
"When it started to rain a little I decided to sit at the pits and wait for it to clear. There was nothing to be gained by going out in it," said Doohan.
"Fortunately for me it stopped just in time and because it was only a light shower the track dried out very quickly."
Criville said he had eased off in the rain because of the danger of crashing.
Both he and Doohan complained of setting-up problems with their bikes that remained unresolved.

"We were struggling against a front-end problem that resulted in me running off the track at one stage this afternoon," said Doohan. "The problem is still there and we shall be working to get it sorted out tomorrow."
Criville said one of his bikes had a gearbox fault while the other had a pin-sized hole in the radiator.

"When I braked at the end of the main straight a little water came on to my leathers but when I stopped at the pits my mechanics couldn't find the cause until they took off all the fairing," the Spaniard said.

"It was a new radiator that we fitted to the machine after I crashed it during practice at Jerez and it could have been on the machine I selected for the race. It was very lucky for me that I decided not to race it."
Italian Luca Cadalora was third fastest, keeping Yamaha in the frame in a Honda-dominated season while Suzuki also got a look-in with sixth fastest Australian Daryl Beattie.
The final qualifying session is on Saturday.
